This case is registered on the basis of charge sheet submitted by ACP Madivala Sub-Division against the accused persons for the offences punishable under Section 69, 3(5) of BNS, 2023 and Spl.C.No:2064/2024 sec.3(1)(w)(i), (w)(ii), 3(2)(v), 3(2)(va), of SC/ST (POA) Act, 1989.

2. The case of the prosecution is that on 05.09.2024 the complainant lodged complaint before the Audogodi police that accused No.1 promised to marry the victim and had physical relationship,
when marriage was asked to be performed the other accused persons abused the victim as she visited their village and asked for the same, on 14.08.2024 they started an altercation and abused the victim.
3. The complainant had made complaint that victim and the accused No.1 were working in HPI Company as associates about 3 years back in the year 2021, accused was a trainer, the accused got acquainted with the victim while giving training through Zoom App. The accused whenever victim found difficulty he used to call her directly and used to meet her gradually they became friends.
Spl
4. The accused on one day had taken up the question of caste and the differences became prominent after that victim was ill-treated by the accused.

After 2 months when the victim was called to attend the office physically accused met her and mentioned she is going to be married very soon then accused mentioned that his brother is there after his marriage he will take consent from his family and marry her.

On 08.08.2022 accused took victim outside her PG in Electronic City and took her to Neeladri Apartment on 09.08.2022 when victim was near Vipro Gate, accused came there and took her to his apartment and he promised to marry her and he had physical relationship with the victim.
After that when the victim questioned about their marriage accused promised if at all they talk now itself about their marriage, the family members may break their marriage.

Accordingly, on Adugodi Ps vs A1 Ranjith on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14369725/
2 30.11.2022 accused took the victim to No.10A, Electronic City, Shushruthinagar, Basavapura, there he promised her to marry and had physical relationship, once Spl.C.No:2064/2024 again on 10.03.2023 he took her to Oyo Flagship Hotel Nexus Mall, Koramangala, there he promised he will not deceive her and once again had sexual relationship.
5.
It is reported that on 17.06.2023 accused took the victim to Dharmasthala and there he promised that he will marry her and took her to a hotel where he had physical relationship.
On 23.09.2023 when elder brother of accused was to marry, he even purchased clothes and mentioned he will obtain consent from his mother about their love.
Once again he took the victim to a hotel near Hosakote Town where victim went there, there she met elder brother of the accused and wife of accused No.1's elder brother.
There they mentioned there is no question of marriage with victim and the accused No.1 and after that they got angry over the victim, she has been sent back.

After that accused No.1 once again took the victim to Iggaluru of Kolar District and Taluk where on 14.08.2024 he did not Spl.C.No:2064/2024 responded for the call of the victim and as such his marriage promise has been broken.
Accordingly, victim without having any alternative reported the same before the jurisdictional police.
Accordingly on the basis of complaint, Investigating Officer registered crime and took up investigation.
On the basis of complaint, the investigating officer on conclusion has filed charge sheet.
6. In fact during the course of bail application of accused No.1, when the victim met the accused No.1, accused No.1 had promised her to marry within 2 months from granting bail.

Accordingly,
accused No.1 was granted bail on 24.10.2024.
Further accused No.1 reported the marriage on 04.11.2024.
The charge sheet copies were furnished to the accused as contemplated under Section 207 of Cr.P.C. Heard before the charge.

As there was sufficient materials available, charges framed,
read over and explained to the accused Spl.C.No:2064/2024 persons in vernacular language and pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
7. At trial, the prosecution got examined complainant as P.W.1, the father of P.W.1 as P.W.2 and mother of P.W.1 as P.W.3 and got exhibited Exs.P.1 to 12 and closed its side.
The material witnesses have turned hostile.
Accordingly, 313 statement of accused persons dispensed.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.
9.

The following points would arise for the determination of this Court are as follows;
POINTS 1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that from 2021 accused No.1 in the HPI.Company was friend with C.W.1 as he is loving her, later on 30.11.2022 took the victim to a Hotel Room No.10A, Electronic City, Shushruthinagar, Basavapura, and pretending to marry her had sexual intercourse with her, again on 10.03.2023 at Flagship Hotel Nexus Mall, Koramangala,
and again on 17.06.2023 took her to Dharmasthala and again on Spl.C.No:2064/2024 23.09.2023 pretending to marry her had sexual intercourse with her and thereby accused has committed offence punishable u/s 69 of BNS 2023?
Adugodi Ps vs A1 Ranjith on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14369725/
3 2.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on 14.08.2024 accused No.1 took the victim to Igaluru village, Maluru told C.W.1 that they will not solemnize marriage of accused No.1 and victim and accused persons not being the members of SC/ST intentionally insulted/intimidated C.W.1 as "     "
with intent to humiliate the C.W.1 who belongs to schedule caste community in a place within the public view and thereby accused has committed offences punishable u/s 3(1)(r) of SC/ST (POA) Act?

3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the aforesaid date, time and place, accused No.1 not being a member of SC/ST, knowing very well that CW1 belongs to Scheduled Caste has intentionally touched her body with sexual nature without her consent and thereby committed offence punishable u/sec 3(1)(w)(i) of SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act?
4. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the afore said date, time and place, the accused No.1 not being a member of SC/ST, knowing very well that CW1 belongs to Scheduled Caste has committed rape on her and thereby committed offence Spl.C.No:2064/2024 punishable u/sec 3(1)(w)(ii) of SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act?
5.

sentences.text: In her examination in chief deposed on 21.11.2024 she and accused No.1 had married as per Hindu Customs and Traditions.
The complainant deposed before the court that accused No.2 is her mother-in-law and accused No.3 is her sister in law, accused No.4 is her husband's elder brother.
She admits signature made on Ex.P.1.
She further deposed that before marriage she had made complaint as accused No.1 refused to marry her.
The victim deposed before the court that she does not remember entire details of the complaint.
This witness deposes she never went to Igaluru, no incident happened and she has not been abused by taking caste name.

Accordingly, she further did not went before the police, however admits Adugodi Ps vs A1 Ranjith on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14369725/
4 signing Ex.P.2 before the jurisdictional Magistrate.
This witness deposes further what are all the statement made by her before the Magistrate is not in her memory, as on this day as she has already married accused No.1.

Accordingly, this witness further deposes about signing Ex.P.3 the spot Mahazar and Ex.P.4 photographs which were Spl.C.No:2064/2024 taken by the Investigating Officer during the course of investigation.
This witness admits her statement before police as per Exs.P.4 and 5 however turns hostile.
The learned SPP has treated this witness as hostile and cross examined, nothing has been elicited so as to support the prosecution case.
12. The PWs.2 and 3 Radha and Narahari are the parents of the victim who depose about the marriage of the victim with accused No.1.
The witnesses depose there is no any untoward incident happened as per the complaint.
The learned counsel for the accused submits accused No.1 as per his conditional bail had married the victim.

However the same with regard to ingredients of offence alleged, there is no proof so as to punish or consider the guilt of the accused No.1, as such, the summoning other material witnesses may be dispensed and the accused have taken the victim as their family member.
In the absence of ingredients of alleged offence, seeks acquittal.
The learned SPP submits offence is not just committed against the victim, however it is an offence committed against the society.
As such, trial is to be conducted and all the material witnesses are to be examined.
The learned counsel for the accused submits they are ready to give consent with regard to caste of the victim and the accused with regard to medical report of accused No.1 is consented.

14. On going through the evidence of the complainant, PWs.2 and 3, it is true the offence punishable u/s.69 of BNS is not punishable offence, however as the marriage of the victim and the accused No.1 being performed which is the crux of allegations made, this court is satisfied to dispense summoning of the Investigating Officer and official witnesses.
In fact the documents with regard to caste report are marked on consent, considering the other offence to incriminate the accused the alleged offence punishable u/s.69 of BNS 2023 is not available.
Accordingly, this court based on the evidence on record Spl.C.No:2064/2024 and the documents marked on consent, is satisfied to answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

15. POINT NO.2: In the case on hand, in proof the ingredients of alleged offence punishable u/s. 3(1)
(r) of SC/ST (POA) Act 1989, the documents with regard to caste report are marked on consent, in the absence of corroboration alleged offence punishable u/s.3(1)(r) of SC/ST (POA) Act 1989 only on the evidence of complainant alone, the guilt of the accused cannot be presumed is my firm view.
Accordingly, this court is satisfied to answer this Point No.2 in the Negative.
16. POINT NOS.3
AND 4:

In the case on hand, with regard to the offence punishable u/s.3(1)(w)(i)
and 3(1)(w)(ii) of SC/ST (POA) Act 1989, this court is satisfied to answer as per the discussion made supra on Point No.1, in the complaint specific allegation has been made by the complainant with regard to accused No.1 touching the victim and having relationship with Spl.

sentences.text: In fact as argued by the learned counsel for the accused, as per the provisions of SC/ST (POA) Act 1989, there is consent with regard to sexual relationship between the victim and the accused No.1.
Therefore it does not amount to any offence.

17. The learned SPP argues as per the provisions of SC/ST (POA) Act 1989, sec.3(1)(w)(i), (ii)
proviso even though there is consent, it amounts to no consent as per the provisions to the above sections.
Therefore it is an offence committed against the accused.

18. This court on going through the charge sheet, documents marked on record and the evidence of the complainant, when the victim and the accused No.1 became husband and wife, the arguments of learned counsel for the accused that it was a consensual sex seems a reasonable prayer.

Accordingly,
considering the entire materials on record, this court is satisfied to answer these Points No.3 and 4 in the Negative.
POINT NO.5:

In the case on hand, in proof of the ingredients of offence punishable u/s.3(2)(v) of SC/ST (POA) Act 1989, it has been alleged that accused has committed schedule offence namely offence punishable u/s.69 of BNS 2023 of IPC, however on considering the entire material on record and evidence, this court had come to the conclusion that prosecution is unable to prove the ingredients of schedule offence being committed by the accused.

Under such circumstances as the alleged offence are punishable upto 10 years, in the absence of proof with regard to the alleged offence, this court independently cannot convict the accused for the above offence unless the IPC offence are proved by the prosecution.

Under such circumstances this court is satisfied to answer this Point No.5 in the Negative.
20. POINT No.6 : The accused persons do complied the provisions of section 437A of Cr.P.C., by providing personal bond before this court, for their Spl.C.No:2064/2024 appearance before the Hon'ble Appellate court.

In view of my foregoing reasons, I proceed the pass the following;
ORDER
Acting under Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused Nos.1 to 4 are acquitted of the offences under Section 69 of BNS, 2023 and sec.3(1)(r), (w)(i), (w)(ii), 3(2)(v), of SC/ST (POA) Act, 1989.
The accused are set at liberty.
However, the bond executed in compliance of Sec.437(A) of Cr.P.C., shall be in force till appeal period.
